  STAFF REPORT

Meeting Date:  September 10, 2026
To:  City Council and Planning Commission Liaison Committee
From:  Huma Ahmed, City Clerk
Subject:  Planning Commission Interviews
Attachments:  Proposed Questions

INTRODUCTION
The Planning Commission Interview Panel will conduct interviews for the Planning
Commission on Thursday, September 10, 2026. The Panel is composed of
Councilmember Lester J. Friedman, Councilmember Sharona R. Nazarian, PsyD,
Planning Commission Chair Lou Milkowski, and Vice Chair Gary Ross.

DISCUSSION
The Planning Commission interviews are being redone due to a technicality identified in
the original interview process.  Please treat this process as if no previous
recommendation had been made and this committee is engaging in this process for the
firsttime.

Members of the public may attend the interviews but may speak only during the
designated public comment period. Once the public comment period has closed,
members of the public may remain as observers.

The following individuals have expressed an interest in serving on the Planning
Commission (alpha order):

  •  Jason Grant
  •  Joshua Greer
  •  Sharon Persovski
  •  Helena Rosenthal
  •  An Tuchman

The Interview Panel may recommend appointing two individuals if there is sufficient
interest in filling a current and an upcoming vacancy. Per the City Council Policy
Handbook, there should be a minimum of three candidates to fill one vacancy and a
minimum of five candidates to fill two vacancies.
 Meeting Date: September 10, 2026

The first vacancy is the seat previously held by Commissioner Myra Demeter, whose
term concluded on June 30, 2026. This seat will be filled through an immediate
appointment. If there is sufficient interest, the second vacancy may be filled for the seat
currently held by Commissioner Gary Ross, whose term is scheduled to conclude on
June 30, 2027. All appointments require City Council formal approval.

FISCAL IMPACT
None.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff is requesting that the City Council and Planning Commission Liaison Committee
conduct interviews with the candidates listed and provide their recommendations for the
Planning Commission.

As is customary, applications have  been  posted  on  the  City’s  website  at
www.beverlyhills.org/commissionapps.

  Huma Ahmed,
  City Clerk
  Approved By

Page 2 of 2
 Attachment 1
   Planning Commission
  Interview Questions

1. What do you believe are the most important land use and planning issues facing
  Beverly Hills over the next 10 to 20 years?

2. State law increasingly limits local discretion over housing approvals, including
  through laws such as SB 79 that affects development near the new subway
  stations. Given these constraints, what do you see as the Planning Commission’s
  role in shaping Beverly Hills’ future growth?

3. Beverly Hills depends on a strong commercial sector while also placing a high
  value on residential quality of life. How should planning policy balance these
  priorities, particularly when such uses are directly adjacent to each other?

4. How do you feel about identifying and managing potential conflicts of interest as
  a Commissioner?

5. What is your perspective on approving projects with significant, unavoidable
  environmental impacts when the City finds the benefits outweigh those impacts?

6. Beverly Hills has significant historic and architecturally notable properties
  alongside ongoing demand for new development. How would you approach
  decisions where preservation goals conflict with redevelopment or increased
  density?

7. How would you approach ensuring that a range of voices, not just the most vocal
  or most actively engaged residents, are heard in the Commission’s process?

  rev. 9/2026
 8. The next Housing Element cycle will require the City to plan for housing capacity
  beyond 2029. What do you see as the key challenges in that process, and how
  would you approach identifying sites and policies to meet the City’s housing
  allocation requirement while addressing community concerns?

9. Beverly Hills serves residents, businesses, employees, and visitors, who may
  experience the City very differently. How should those different perspectives
  inform planning decisions?

10.Planning decisions made today can have effects that last for decades. How
  would you distinguish between short-term concerns and the City’s long-term
  interests when considering an issue before the Commission?

CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 N. Rexford Drive

  Beverly Hills, CA 90210

  Beverly Hills City Council and
  Planning Commission Liaison Committee Special Meeting

  Thursday, September 10, 2026
  4:00 PM

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER: Date/Time: Thursday, September 10 at 4:00PM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Councilmember Lester J. Friedman, Councilmember
  Sharona R. Nazarian, PsyD, PC Chair Lou Milkowski and PC Vice
  Chair Gary Ross, Assistant City Manager Stephanie Harris and
  City Clerk Huma Ahmed, with members of the public

1) PUBLIC COMMENT
  a) Members of the public will be given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on
  any item listed on the agenda.

  -  Jordan Rubinstein re: Applicant Support

2) Planning Commission Interview Panel will conduct interviews for new member(s) of
  the Planning Commission and make recommendations for appointment.

Councilmember Friedman opened the meeting and reviewed the ground rules. The purpose of
the meeting was to cure and correct the interview process in accordance with the Brown Act. The
process was to be conducted de novo in a manner that disregards any previous recommendations
of the committee, which are repealed, and the interviews will be approached as a new process.

Proposed interview questions were included in the packet. The panel divided up the questions
and agreed to ask them in the same order to each candidate. Five eligible applications were
received, but four candidates confirmed their participation for the interviews.

The following candidates interviewed with the panel:

  •  Sharon Persovski
  •  Ari Tuchman
  •  Joshua Greer
  •  Jason Grant

  1 | Page
 September 10, 2026

Upon conclusion of the interviews, the panel deliberated in a public setting and recommended the
following:

  1. Jason Grant was recommended for appointment to fill the seat held by former
  Commissioner Myra Demeter, her term concluded on June 30, 2026.

  Pending City Council approval, his appointment will be effective immediately; however,
  because this is a mid-term appointment, his initial term will be approximately three
  months short of a full two-year initial term.

  2. Joshua Greer is recommended to be appointed to fill the upcoming vacancy for
  Commissioner Gary Ross’ seat which is scheduled to conclude on June 30, 2027.

  3. The staff report will be provided at the September 22, 2026, Study Session meeting, and
  with City Council approval also formally approved on Consent during the evening Formal
  Session meeting on the same day.

3) Adjournment
  There being no further feedback or discussion, Councilmember Friedman adjourned the
  meeting at 6:00PM.
